target_customer: Independent filmmakers and creators making AI films
problem: AI video tools give little director control; Flick offers a node canvas for scripts, scenes, characters and edits, plus a distribution platform, Flick TV.
business_model: Subscription software plans plus a content platform

founders.name: Ray Wang
founders.background_notes: YC page: founding engineer on Instagram's AI team

founders.name: Zoey Zhang
founders.background_notes: YC page: filmmaker and product designer; SIGGRAPH 2025 paper

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating generative video models with character consistency and a node editor is demanding.

defensibility.rationale: Filmmaker community and Flick TV could build loyalty, but underlying models come from third parties and tools like Runway and LTX compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Model vendors and competitors offer overlapping canvas tools in 2026 roundups; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: AI filmmaking was growing quickly in 2025; the founders met while making Zhang's AI film in April 2025 per the press release.

identity.voice_and_tone: Filmmaker-first, positioned as Figma plus Cursor for AI filmmaking

branding.brand_signature: Flick TV, festival and filmmaker residency
branding.community_and_virality: Runs an AI film festival, a filmmaker residency with 17 short films and an MIT AI Film Hack partnership.

brand_strength.rationale: Active community programs (residency, festival, TV) tie into the brand, though the name is a common word.

outcome_analysis: Flick raised a $6M seed in May 2026 from True Ventures, GV and others after YC. It combines an Instagram engineer with an award-winning AI filmmaker and builds community through residencies, a festival and Flick TV. Competition from larger AI video tools is the main risk. No exit.
notes: Startupintros lists a $500K seed in Aug 2025, unverified and not recorded. Dated competitor search returned only 2026 roundups, so the list is empty. Education not found.
